missing: Scott 2016 full text is retrievable (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4867749/); the draft's dose/engagement judgements say it was not. It states rodent-vs-human comparisons for lymphocyte kinetics and for efficacy (cites TOUCHSTONE), and predicts 'limited effects on heart rate and no effect on QT interval prolongation' from S1P3-sparing - the in-context safety prediction for ozanimod.

In-context safety contradiction for the UC drugs: Tran 2017 (10.1002/jcph.887, ozanimod FIH) 'A dose-dependent negative chronotropic effect was observed following the first dose'; Lee 2024 (10.1002/cpdd.1379, etrasimod SAD/MAD) 'mean reductions seen after the first dose of up to 19.5 bpm'. Both healthy volunteers, both verified at abstract level; neither states the mouse comparison. Patient-level bradycardia in TRUE NORTH (10.1056/NEJMoa2033617) / ELEVATE (10.1016/S0140-6736(23)00061-2) not checked.

Amiselimod UC phase 2 NCT04857112: no registry results or paper (confirmed), but Bausch Health press release 2023-12-21 reports primary endpoint met (modified Mayo -2.3 vs -1.6, p=0.002; remission 32.4% vs 17.8%). Same direction as the CD45RBhi/IL-10-/- models; not a primary source under rule 1, so no status change, but the judgement text should carry it and watch for the publication.

model_filed is null in every entry: the Zeposia FDA pharmacology review (accessdata.fda.gov, NDA 209899) was not consulted for whether the TNBS/CD45RBhi colitis models or S1P3 data were filed. Not checked here (budget).
rule_questions: safety contra 2012: Gergely 2012 is the only stated comparison in the draft, but siponimod was never a UC drug and the subjects were healthy volunteers in an MS programme. Does 'a drug in this context' (contra rule) mean drug-of-class (then 2012 stands) or drug-in-this-disease (then contra moves to 2017 via Tran 2017, juxtaposed with Sanna 2004 and Scott 2016's 'limited effects on heart rate'; or to 2021 if patients are required)? My call: 2012 stands - the prediction is receptor-level class pharmacology, indication-independent, and the pivotal ozanimod paper relied on the same S1P3 argument; fact fields already record the proxy.

same via juxtaposition: engagement 2 and efficacy 2 cite Sandborn 2016 with comparison_stated false. The checker brief says same without a published comparison should be untested; the v2 drafter brief tolerates juxtaposition and records it. Moot here only because Scott 2016 itself states both comparisons - decide whether src should move to Scott 2016 (comparison_stated true, subjects healthy_volunteers for engagement) or stay on the patient trial.

dose cell: Scott 2016 states a rodent half-life -> once-daily prediction that held in humans (19 h). If a regimen prediction counts as the 'exposure/occupancy target', dose becomes same 2016 (direction_only, comparison stated, healthy volunteers); the draft's untested assumes an exposure-target test is required.

contra 'overrides every matched status': the safety judgement reasons that amiselimod's replacement model 'does not lift the contra' because amiselimod lacks a UC result. Under the rule nothing lifts a contra, so the amiselimod argument is moot - unless the atlas intends a later entry to show a replacement model that matched (Sugahara 2017 / Harada 2017, not verified here).
